## 0.6.4 (2026-11-06)


### Release Highlights

- **🚨 Breaking change: this release does not work with older versions, projects or tickets.** It does not convert data from an earlier version. On first start it refuses an older database, leaves it untouched and names the files to delete, and older projects and tickets must be started fresh. Read [Data from an earlier version](https://www.looptroop.ovh/docs/installation#data-from-an-earlier-version) before you upgrade.
- **🚀 LoopTroop — What's New Since v0.6.3**
- A speed update: the server stays responsive while the board refreshes and ticket sizes are calculated, startup is quicker, and logs open and scroll much faster.
- **1. ⚡ A board that no longer stalls** — Refreshing the board, opening a ticket page or calculating a ticket's size no longer freezes the server, so "backend not available" stops appearing during normal use.
- **2. 🚀 Ready sooner after a restart** — Startup reads only what it needs: the end of each log file, tickets by ID, and the OpenCode sessions that still exist. On a machine with 55 tickets it went from 41 s to under 20 s.
- **3. 📜 Logs that open and scroll quickly** — On a long ticket, the coding phase's Activity panel loads in about a second instead of 5–6 seconds, and scrolling back through the Debug log no longer re-sorts the whole history for every page.
- **4. 🧹 Smaller log files** — Each log line stores its text once. Normal and AI logs are about half their previous size and the debug log about a third, with no change to what the log views show.
- **5. 🔧 Less background work** — Ticket pages check for a ticket with one lookup, board refreshes skip artifact loading they do not need, and Git settings are reused for five seconds instead of starting an extra process for every command.
- **✨ Overall:** the same app, much faster, but it needs a fresh start.

### Summary

- The server stays responsive while the board refreshes, ticket pages load and ticket sizes are calculated, so "backend not available" no longer appears during normal use.
- LoopTroop is ready sooner after a restart.
- Log panels open several times faster on long tickets, scrolling back through the Debug log no longer freezes the app, and log files take about half the space.
- **Breaking:** data from earlier versions is no longer upgraded. Start fresh: LoopTroop refuses an older database and says what to delete.

### Performance

- Board refreshes no longer load every AI artifact of every ticket to find its Manual QA records; the database returns only those records. A 55-ticket board refresh went from about 2.2 s to under 1 s, and every ticket page that builds a ticket summary benefits too.
- Tickets that have no ticket folder (finished tickets whose worktree was deleted, and display-only demo tickets) no longer run `git` on every refresh to find their base branch. The answer is kept per project for 30 seconds; tickets with a folder still detect and store it as before.
- The open-questions check that runs every 30 seconds lists open tickets straight from the database instead of building the whole board first, so it no longer stalls the server for seconds at a time.
- Ticket routes that only need to know a ticket exists (artifacts, artifact manifest and content, saved UI state, interview, AI details, beads, files, execution setup, per-ticket questions) now check that with one database lookup instead of assembling the full ticket.
- Calculating a ticket's size reads each folder once, with a limited number of file reads at a time, instead of re-reading every folder once per level above it. The server stays responsive while it runs; a 25,000-file worktree went from 24 s to 7 s.
- Startup checks the end of each log file for a torn last line instead of reading whole logs, skips the package caches kept under `runtime/execution-setup` when it looks for interrupted writes, and lists tickets by ID instead of building them. On a machine with 55 tickets, startup work fell from 41 s to under 20 s.
- Startup asks OpenCode once which sessions it still has, then checks only those for leftover AI questions, up to eight at a time. It used to ask about every session it ever recorded, one after another; on a machine with 1,144 recorded sessions, 92% no longer existed.
- Streamed AI text is only sent to the screen, never saved, but every streamed chunk used to look up its ticket and resolve its file paths first. That work now happens only for lines that are saved. Each streaming model cost 15–33% of the server's time; council phases, where several models stream at once, no longer slow the app down.
- Saving a log line resolves only the log file it writes to, the log cache looks its ticket up once per line, and control characters are removed from log text in one pass. A multi-megabyte AI message is now logged in well under half the time.
- Log views no longer read every stored entry's full text to decide which rows to show: the fields they filter and sort on are stored as columns when an entry is indexed, with the full entry kept last in the row. On a long ticket, the coding phase's Activity panel loads in about a second instead of 5–6 seconds, and the Overview in a fraction of a second.
- The Debug log reads each page straight off an index in its own order. Scrolling back used to re-sort the ticket's whole debug history for every page (1–2 s per page, up to 20 s for some); a page now takes a few milliseconds to find.
- The Activity panel loads 500 entries per request instead of 200, so a long phase needs half as many requests.
- Ticket screens load only the artifacts they show. The verification summary, the PRD and beads approval panes and the coverage progress title ask for the few artifact types or the one phase they read, and the artifacts panel loads its own source phases, the same ones the review and council views pass it, instead of every artifact the ticket ever produced (11–17 MB on a long ticket).
- The artifact manifest and the live `artifact_change` events reuse each artifact version's size, hash and preview instead of hashing and parsing every artifact again on each request.
- A board refresh looks each project and the settings profile up once instead of once per ticket, and finds a ticket's latest artifact of a given type through an index on ticket and artifact type.
- Every git command used to start a second `git config` process first, to check for a custom `core.sshCommand`. That answer is now reused for five seconds per repository, which halves the git processes LoopTroop starts; a changed setting still takes effect within those seconds.
- The board parses a ticket's bead file again only when the file changes, so a bead file with entries it cannot use is reported once per change instead of on every refresh.

### Added

- `GET /api/tickets/:id/artifacts` and `GET /api/tickets/:id/artifacts/manifest` accept repeatable exact `type` filters (`?type=prd_votes&type=prd_drafts`), alone or with `phase`.

### Fixed

- Question wait timers left open by a restart are closed at startup again. A session OpenCode no longer had counted as an unverified check, and one such session stopped startup from closing leftover timers for its whole project, so those tickets kept counting the downtime as waiting time in their duration and ETA. Sessions that reconnected are always checked, and the list of sessions OpenCode still has is trusted only when it is complete for every project (OpenCode v2); with OpenCode v1, or when the list fails or is cut short, every recorded session is checked as before.
- With OpenCode v1, an HTTP error from the session list is reported as an error instead of being read as a server with no sessions.
- `looptroop doctor` no longer reports a refused database as fixed when it cannot be read, and it stops reporting a refusal once the installed LoopTroop can open that database (it used to compare against the version that recorded the refusal).
- The Bead Commits view of a finished Coding phase shows its Net Diff (the final candidate diff), which the Coding phase review left empty.

### Changed

- Canceling a ticket deletes its execution setup folder, with the package caches setup downloaded (these can reach gigabytes), once the cancel is confirmed. The delete runs without blocking the server, and the next start retries any folder a canceled ticket left behind. Completed tickets already lose this folder in Cleaning Up; blocked tickets keep it, so a retry can reuse the cache.
- Log files store each text once. A line's `content` is left out when it is the same as its `message`, and a debug line keeps its payload only in `data` instead of also writing it out as text. Log views, exports and downloads show exactly the same text as before. The normal and AI logs are about half their previous size and the debug log about a third, and the log cache in the project database shrinks the same way. Tools that read the log files directly should use `message` when `content` is absent, and for a line marked `payloadInData` the text is its `message` followed by `data` (without `timestamp`) as JSON.
- `daemon.json`, which `looptroop status --json` reports, records a refused start with `schema.resetInstructions` (what to delete) in place of `schema.migratableFrom`, and `schema.databaseLabel` is now required. `looptroop doctor --json` adds `databaseLabel` and, for an older database, `resetInstructions` to its `schema` facts.

### Removed

- **Breaking:** LoopTroop no longer upgrades data from earlier versions. Both databases moved to schema version 3, and a database written by any other version is refused at startup, untouched, with a message that says what to delete to start fresh. `looptroop doctor` reports an older app database as a failure with the same steps, where it used to promise an automatic upgrade.
- The old git hook policy names (`validate_explicitly`, `ignore_internal_only`, `use_on_internal_commits`) are no longer translated when settings, projects or setup plans are read.
- Other readers of data written by earlier versions are gone too: version 1 skip receipts and Manual QA fix-bead files, interview claims without a boot ID, temp files named by the old atomic writer, the `.cache/project-tooling` setup cache that bead commits used to skip, the browser's old per-project preset keys, `onlyErrors` filter and `logs-` log keys, and the log viewer's filtering of summary lines older versions wrote.
